# 7-day sample menu: stage 3, no dialysis

--8<-- "includes/starting-points.md"

This week shows how stage 3 kidney disease with type 1 diabetes can look on the plate: three meals with about 55 g of carbohydrate each, small snacks, about 56 g of protein (0.8 g per kg for a 70 kg adult), sodium well under 2,000 mg and no foods with phosphate additives. Potassium and phosphorus stay well under the stage 3 review ceilings without counting every fruit, because at stage 3 they are limited only if your blood tests run high. Drink to thirst: there is no fluid limit before dialysis unless your team sets one.

## The numbers this menu is built to

Built for a reference adult: 70 kg, 170 cm, type 1 diabetes, using the app's starting targets for **G3b** (see [Eating well](../index.md#your-numbers)). Every day below was checked against these numbers by `scripts/build_handbook.py`.

| Per day | Built to |
|---|---|
| Protein | about 56 g (0.8 g/kg); days stay within 56–58.8 g |
| Potassium | at most 3,500 mg |
| Phosphorus | at most 1,000 mg |
| Sodium | at most 2,000 mg |
| Energy from food | 1,750–2,450 kcal |
| Carbohydrate | about 55 g at each main meal (every meal 50–60 g); snacks 10–30 g |

Also: no foods with phosphate additives.

## Swaps that keep the numbers

- **Oatmeal for Cream of Wheat** (1 cup): about +125 mg potassium, +140 mg phosphorus and +2.7 g fiber. Fine at stage 3 when your potassium and phosphate results are in range.
- **Whole-wheat for white bread:** about +45 mg potassium and +40 mg phosphorus per slice, with twice the fiber.
- **Brown rice for white** (1 cup): about +120 mg potassium, +140 mg phosphorus and +2.6 g fiber.
- **Fruit:** any ½ cup of applesauce, blueberries, strawberries, raspberries, grapes or canned pears or peaches can replace another, but check the carbohydrate: ½ cup of grapes is about 14 g, strawberries about 6 g.
- **Protein foods:** chicken, turkey, pork loin, cod and pot roast swap ounce for ounce for potassium; salmon and tilapia have more (about 330 mg per 3 oz).

## Make it yours

- **Scale for your weight.** Protein here is 0.8 g per kg for 70 kg. At 60 kg that is about 48 g a day, at 80 kg about 64 g: shrink or grow the meat at lunch and dinner by about ½ oz for each 5 kg. Ask your dietitian which weight to use.
- **Carbohydrate stays steady:** about the same amount at each main meal every day, so a fixed insulin plan or a carbohydrate ratio works the same way from day to day. Your own amount per meal comes from your diabetes team; keep it consistent and count what you actually eat ([Carb counting](../carb-counting.md)).
- **Lows come first.** Treat a low straight away with glucose tablets or another fast 15 g ([Treating a low](../../t1d/treating-a-low.md)), even if it adds potassium or fluid. Rescue foods are on top of these menus and are never "against the rules".
- **Hungry, or losing weight without trying?** Add calories with olive oil, unsalted butter or more measured starch covered by your usual insulin plan, not with more meat, and tell your dietitian ([Eating enough](../eating-enough.md)).
- **Season without salt:** herbs, spices, garlic and onion powder, lemon and vinegar. Do not use salt substitutes: they contain potassium chloride ([Sodium](../sodium.md)).
- **Log it in the app:** every food here is in the app's food list under the same name. Saved meals and "copy day" let you reuse a menu day ([Planning and menus](../../app/planning-and-menus.md)).

## Sources

- [USDA FoodData Central (SR Legacy)][FDC]: every nutrient value, through the app's food list.
- [KDOQI 2020 nutrition guideline][Q20]: energy 25–35 kcal/kg (statement 3.1.1) and protein (statements 3.0.1–3.0.4).
- [KDIGO 2024 CKD guideline][K24]: sodium under 2 g a day (Rec 3.3.2.1); protein 0.8 g/kg at G3–G5 (Rec 3.3.1.1); limit bioavailable potassium only when it runs high (PP 3.11.5.2).
- [ADA Standards of Care 2026, section 11][A26-11]: protein 0.8 g/kg with diabetes and CKD before dialysis, 1.0–1.2 g/kg on dialysis (Rec 11.3).
- [ADA Standards of Care 2026, section 5][A26-5]: consistent carbohydrate in time and amount for people on fixed insulin plans (Rec 5.28).
- [NKF: carbohydrate counting with CKD][DG7]: 15 g is one carbohydrate choice; 3–6 choices per meal, set by your dietitian.
- [Bethke and Jansky 2008][DG6]: boiling small pieces of potato removes about half its potassium (Day 3).
